title: Sections with support: derived adjunction and fiber formula
statement:
In the situation of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves], let
$R\underline\Gamma_Z\colon\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$ be the
right derived functor of $\underline\Gamma_Z$, computed on K-injective
complexes.

1. $R\underline\Gamma_Z$ is right adjoint to
   $i_*\colon\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)\to\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, and for
   $A\in\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, $K\in\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$
   $$
   R\operatorname{Hom}_X(i_*A,K)\simeq R\operatorname{Hom}_Z(A,R\underline\Gamma_ZK).
   $$
2. For an injective $\Lambda_X$-module $I$, the unit $I\to j_*j^*I$ is surjective.
3. There is a distinguished triangle, natural in $K$,
   $$
   i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK\longrightarrow K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\longrightarrow i_*R\underline\Gamma_ZK[1]
   $$
   in $\D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda)$, whose second arrow is the unit of $j^*\dashv Rj_*$.
   Consequently
   $$
   R\underline\Gamma_ZK\simeq i^*\fib\bigl(K\longrightarrow Rj_*j^*K\bigr)\quad\text{in }\D(Z_{\mathrm{proét}},\Lambda).
   $$

proof.text: The standing setting [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting] makes $X$ finite type over a field. By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] choose a finite affine cover $X=\bigcup_{r=1}^m\operatorname{Spec}A_r$ with each $A_r$ a finitely generated algebra over that field. By [lem-wf-affine-noetherian-components], descending chains of closed subsets in each chart stabilize, equivalently ascending chains of open subsets stabilize. Consequently every union of opens in a chart is a finite subunion: the finite subunions have a maximal element, since otherwise one could recursively construct a strictly increasing chain. In particular every open subset of a chart is quasi-compact, and every open subset of $X$ is quasi-compact by this finite cover. This also proves that $j$ is quasi-compact: its inverse image of any affine open of $X$ is an open subset of $X$. Finally every inverse image of an affine open under the diagonal $X\to X\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}X$ is open in $X$, hence quasi-compact, so $X$ is quasi-separated by [def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism]. Thus the qcqs and quasi-compact-complement hypotheses used below follow from the inherited setting.

source.place: standing-scheme hypotheses for the open--closed operations in clauses (1)--(3)

proof.text: Apply clauses (2) and (3) of the existing broader statement [det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction]. The admissible coefficient ring is a condensed ring, the closed immersion is the given $i$, and step 1 verifies quasi-compactness of its open complement. Its support functor is exactly $M\mapsto i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ from [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves], with the same inverse-image coefficient rings. Its derived functor is computed on K-injectives, just as in the present statement. Clause (2) therefore gives both the derived adjunction and the global $R\operatorname{Hom}$ isomorphism of assertion (1), on the whole unbounded derived categories. Clause (3) gives assertion (2): the particular sheaf adjunction unit $I\to j_*j^*I$ is surjective for every injective $I$. This application uses neither a constructibility restriction nor constant discrete coefficients. We will construct the triangle rather than infer the identity of its middle map from the unlabeled arrows in that node's clause (4).

source.place: clauses (1) and (2); the unit proof also explicitly cites det-lem-formal-closed-support-adjunction

proof.text:
The module-sheaf categories on $X,Z,V$, over their actual pulled-back ring sheaves, are Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], taking the small site models in the fixed common universe. Apply [lem-pur-kinjective-degreewise-existence] to resolve an arbitrary, possibly unbounded complex $K$ by $K\to I$, with $I$ K-injective and every $I^n$ injective. Assertion (3) of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves] makes $H(I)$ K-injective, where $H=\underline\Gamma_Z$, and [def-sfb-right-derived-functor] identifies it with $RHK$. With $B=\Lambda_X$, clause (1) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] gives exact $j_!\dashv j^*$ and exact $j^*$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $v=j_!$, $u=j^*$; thus $j^*I$ is K-injective and $j^*K\to j^*I$ is a quasi-isomorphism. It follows that $Rj_*j^*K$ is represented by $j_*j^*I$. Assertion (1) of the sheaf-support node identifies the kernel of the unit in each degree with $i_*H(I^n)$; step 2 gives surjectivity in each degree. Hence there is a natural degreewise short exact sequence of complexes
$$0\longrightarrow i_*H(I)\longrightarrow I\xrightarrow{\eta_I}j_*j^*I\longrightarrow0.$$
The kernel identifications commute with the differentials by their naturality. No choice of splittings enters this sequence.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-triangle] to the sequence of step 3. Exactness of $i_*$ is assertion (2) of [det-lem-formal-closed-support-sheaves]; by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] its degreewise application computes its derived action. Thus the triangle's terms are $i_*RHK$, $K$, and $Rj_*j^*K$. Its second arrow is the map represented by the sheaf unit $\eta_I$. This is specifically the derived unit: apply the termwise adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy] to $j^*\dashv j_*$ from [def-sfb-module-upper-lower-adjunction]. Since $j^*$ is exact, [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] with $v=j^*$ and $u=j_*$ makes $j_*j^*I$ K-injective as well. The Hom comparison [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] then identifies the derived Hom adjunction with the homotopy adjunction on these representatives; the identity of $j^*I$ corresponds to $\eta_I$, proving the claim about the unit. The connecting arrow is natural for chain maps by the short-exact-sequence triangle node. Every derived morphism between $K,K'$ is represented by a homotopy class of maps between their K-injective resolutions, by the same Hom comparison. The additive termwise functors $i_*H$, identity, and $j_*j^*$ preserve homotopies explicitly: if $f-g=d_{I'}h+hd_I$, then for any of these functors $F$ additivity and preservation of composition give $F(f)-F(g)=d_{F(I')}F(h)+F(h)d_{F(I)}$. Thus the three component maps depend only on the derived morphism. Therefore the naturality of the connecting arrow descends to the derived categories, giving the natural triangle of assertion (3).

proof.text:
Write $A=i_*RHK$, $B=K$, $C=Rj_*j^*K$, and $g:B\to C$ for the verified unit. By TR2 in [def-weil-triangulated-category], rotate the triangle of step 4 to $B\xrightarrow{g}C\to A[1]\to B[1]$. The representative $\eta_I$ of $g$ has the distinguished cone triangle $B\xrightarrow{g}C\to\operatorname{cone}(\eta_I)\to B[1]$ by [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. TR3 supplies a morphism between these triangles whose first two components are identities; [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso] makes its third component an isomorphism. Shifting by $[-1]$ gives $A\simeq\operatorname{cone}(\eta_I)[-1]=\operatorname{fib}(g)$. This is an isomorphism with the fiber of the specified unit; no functorial choice of cones in an arbitrary triangulated category is being used. Apply $i^*$, which is exact on the actual ring-sheaf modules by clause (2) of [det-sf-open-closed-pullback-limits] and hence acts termwise on derived categories by [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated]. Clause (2) of [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] gives $i^*i_*\cong\mathrm{id}$ on these modules; applying its natural counit termwise gives the same identity on complexes and derived categories. We obtain
$$RHK\simeq i^*i_*RHK\simeq i^*\operatorname{fib}(K\to Rj_*j^*K),$$
which is the required fiber formula. The inverse-image coefficients are exactly those fixed in the sheaf-support statement throughout.

split_report.summary: Rechecked the earlier sandbox and reused the broader existing support theorem only for its explicit adjunction and injective-surjectivity clauses. Proved quasi-compactness from the standing finite-type hypotheses, then constructed the natural triangle on injective-term K-injective resolutions and checked that its middle arrow is the derived adjunction unit. No statement change and no new nodes. Independent second reading made the homotopy equation explicit and supplied the rotation, triangle comparison and existing two-isomorphisms lemma for the fiber identification.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 verifies inherited geometric hypotheses; step 2 realizes clauses (1) and (2) through the broader node explicitly cited in the unit; steps 3--5 realize clause (3) by the original injective-resolution, short-exact-sequence and exact i^* route.

tool_uses.why: The unit explicitly cites this all-coefficient support adjunction as its tool. Clauses (2)--(3) give derived adjunction, global RHom and injective-unit surjectivity; no new node is needed for those already-stated facts.
Its descending-chain condition for finite-type affine charts supplies the elementary compactness argument; this support unit does not prove Hilbert basis/Noetherianity.
Generic ringed-site module categories are Grothendieck, needed to apply unbounded K-injective existence.
Generic Grothendieck-category injective-term K-injective resolutions for unbounded complexes, not a support theorem.
General exact-left-adjoint criterion applies to both j_! and j^*, needed to identify the derived unit on resolutions.
General functorial triangle of a short exact sequence of complexes, needed after the support sequence has been constructed.
Generic passage of exact additive functors to derived categories, used for exact i_* and i^*.
Generic adjunction on homotopy categories including its specified unit, needed to check which triangle arrow is the derived unit.
General homotopy-to-derived Hom bijection, needed to verify the unit and descend naturality.

Generic open–closed operations for modules over the actual sheaf of rings: step 3 uses exact j_! left adjoint to exact j^*, and step 5 uses the counit i^*i_* ≅ id. This is the ring-sheaf form of the unit’s stipulated open–closed input, not a replacement localization proof.
